kernel.governing_law: Absence transfigures the absent one into a cosmic presence; the beloved's distance activates a radiance that saturates the sensory world, yet the longing body remains trapped in its finitude — and the poem's own voice breaks under the weight of what it cannot bridge.
kernel.mutated_relation: The conditions of the utterance surfaced: what must already be true for each predication to be spoken — the prior states, the structural prerequisites, the unsaid architecture that makes each line sayable.
kernel.beats:
Sardis -> a name she cannot stop placing in her mouth
she often turns her thoughts toward you -> something has made you survivable as an image
like a goddess -> a scale exists between what you are and what can be worshipped
she loved your song like no other -> a voice had to leave a body for the hearing to begin
now she shines among Lydian women -> a surrounding must dim for a figure to take light
like the rose-fingered moon -> the sky had to empty first
in the night -> something was removed and called darkness
outshines all other stars -> each star had to agree to be lesser, which is: to be named second
its silver light -> a metal had to be found that could stand for softness without breaking
spreading over salt -> the water had to be still enough to accept what falls on it
heavy sea -> weight is what water carries when no one is crossing it
over the blossom -> the field had to have already opened without being asked
thick meadows -> density is what happens when nothing is picked
the grass weeps -> a surface had to cool below the air to draw moisture down
lovely dew -> beauty had to attach to the involuntary
the roses open wide -> a temperature had to hold through the night without dropping
beside flowering melilot and chervil -> lesser things had to be named to prove the attention was indiscriminate
how many times has she wandered -> a path had to fail to lead anywhere for the walking to become grief
aimlessly -> purpose had to be withdrawn from her like a hand
remembering gentle Atthis -> a gentleness had to have existed first, then been taken into storage
longing gnaws -> a hunger had to find no food and turn on the one who carries it
at her fragile heart -> the organ had to have already thinned from previous use
this mind sings -> a thought had to become unbearable before it turned to music
to go there -> a there had to exist that the body has no method of reaching
it's not easy for us -> a limit had to be discovered by attempting to exceed it
to be like goddesses in loveliness of form -> a form had to fail, and the failure had to be witnessed
Aphrodite -> a power had to exist that does not need permission
poured nectar from her golden hands -> a substance had to exist that the mortal throat can receive but not produce
persuasion -> a resistance had to exist first, or there is nothing to persuade
desire -> desire (RETAIN: desire is already the condition-of-itself; it requires nothing prior but generates all that follows)
I will come -> a distance had to be measured and accepted as crossable

independent.recovered_law: Text A presents imagery and emotional experience as direct lyric states (the moon shines, the grass weeps dew, longing gnaws), while Text B converts every image and state into a precondition or prerequisite that had to be fulfilled ('a surface had to cool,' 'a path had to fail to lead anywhere'), transforming the poem from immediate experience into a causal/logical chain of necessary conditions for that experience to exist.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same transformation: converting direct lyric statements into their underlying preconditions/prerequisites — surfacing what must already be true for each predication to be utterable.
independent.terminal_note: The final portion of Text B maintains the prerequisite/precondition structure ('a power had to exist,' 'a substance had to exist,' 'a distance had to be measured') through to the end.
